'''Nikoloz Tskitishvili''' ({{lang-ka|ნიკოლოზ ცქიტიშვილი}}; born April 14, 1983) is a Georgian former professional [[basketball]] player. At 7 feet tall, he played as [[power forward]]-[[center (basketball)|center]]. Tskitishvili was selected fifth overall by the [[Denver Nuggets]] in the [[2002 NBA draft]]. He also played for the senior [[Georgian national basketball team]].

==Professional career==

===Europe===
From January to July 2002, Tskitishvili played in Italy, for [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]], winning the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] championship under head coach [[Mike D'Antoni]]. He played in 13 games, averaging 6.6 points per game (with a high of 15). Around that time, he was selected as the 5th overall pick of the [[2002 NBA draft]].

===NBA===
On February 25, 2005, Tskitishvili was traded by the [[Denver Nuggets|Nuggets]], to the [[Golden State Warriors]], along with [[Rodney White]], in exchange for [[Eduardo Nájera]], [[Luis Flores (basketball)|Luis Flores]], and a 2007 future first-round draft pick. In three seasons with the Nuggets, Tskitishvili averaged 3.8 points and 1.9 rebounds per game, and shot 30 percent from the field, while appearing in 143 total games.

After playing just 12 games for the Warriors, he signed as a free agent with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], after playing on their [[NBA Summer League]] team. He was traded half-way through the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], to the [[Phoenix Suns]], in exchange for a second-round draft pick.

Tskitishvili's final NBA game was Game 4 of the 2006 Western Conference Finals on May 30, 2006, in a 106–86 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Tskitishvili only played for a minute and half (substituting at the very end of the game for Leandro Barbosa) and recorded no stats. Phoenix would go on to lose games 5 and 6 (with Tskitishvili not playing in either game), thus losing the series to Dallas 4 - 2.

On June 30, 2006, Tskitishvili was claimed off of waivers by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was waived five days later, after the team announced they would re-sign center [[Joel Przybilla]]. On October 2, 2006, Tskitishvili was signed by the [[New York Knicks]], and he was later waived by them on October 25.

With career averages of 2.9 points and 1.8 rebounds per game, over his first four [[NBA]] seasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/nikoloz_tskitishvili/career_stats.html|title=NBA.com player profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130516092545/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/nikoloz_tskitishvili/career_stats.html|archive-date=May 16, 2013}}</ref> Tskitishvili is widely considered to be a major [[draft bust]]. Former [[ESPN]] writer [[Bill Simmons]] claimed that Tskitishvili is "the worst-case scenario for any foreign pick" in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=simmons/070523 | title = Welcome to the next decade of discontent|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 29, 2007}}</ref> Columnist David Schoenfield of [[ESPN]]'s Page 2, ranked Tskitishvili 30th, on his "100 worst draft picks ever", in 2006,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=schoenfield/060427|title=The 100 Worst Draft Picks Ever|work=ESPN.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> and in 2008, ESPN's Adam Reisinger rated Tskitishvili as the worst NBA draft lottery pick ever selected.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=worstpicks/080625|title=They didn't win the lottery with these picks|date=June 26, 2008|work=ESPN.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Europe===
After playing in the [[NBA]], Tskitishvili returned to Europe. In Europe, he had playing stints in the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] ([[CB Sevilla|Caja San Fernando]], [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]], [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|Lagun Aro GBC]]), [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]] ([[Teramo Basket]]), and [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] ([[Panionios BC|Panionios]]). After that, he left Europe and went to Asia, in order to continue his playing career.

===Asia===
While playing in Iran, Tskitishvili won an [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]] championship in 2012, with [[Mahram Tehran BC|Mahram]]. He started the 2012–13 season with Iran's [[Foolad Mahan Isfahan BC|Foolad Mahan Esfahan]], but he was released in November 2012. The next month, he signed with [[Champville SC|Champville]], from Lebanon's [[Lebanese Basketball League|Division A]], and posted 17.9 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks per game, in 27 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/nikoloz-tskitishvili-joins-al-sharjah/|title=Nikoloz Tskitishvili joins Al Sharjah|date=September 30, 2013|work=Court-Side.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On October 27, 2014, he signed for a second stint with Champville.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/139043/lebanese-team-champville-signing-nikoloz-tskitishvili.html|title=Lebanese team Champville signing Nikoloz Tskitishvili|date=October 27, 2014|work=Sportando.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

===NBA comeback attempt===
On September 25, 2015, Tskitishvili signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], returning to the [[NBA]], after a nine-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-luc-mbah-moute-and-nikoloz-tskitishvili|title=L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN MBAH A MOUTE AND TSKITISHVILI|date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Clippers, on October 3, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/la-clippers-waive-tskitishvili|title=L.A. CLIPPERS WAIVE TSKITISHVILI|date=October 3, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 3, 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Asia===
On October 11, 2015, Tskitishvili signed with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/424268/Fujian-lands-Nikoloz-Tskitishvili|title=Fujian lands Nikoloz Tskitishvili|date=October 11, 2015|work=Asia-Basket.com|access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> However, he left the team before the season began, and signed with the Japanese club, [[Link Tochigi Brex]], on November 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/426742/Tochigi-Brex-signs-Nikoloz-Tskitishvili|title=Tochigi Brex signs Nikoloz Tskitishvili|date=November 2, 2015|work=Asia-Basket.com|access-date=November 19, 2015}}</ref> On December 24, he left Tochigi Brex, after averaging eight points and four rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/185932/nikoloz-tskitishvili-leaves-tochigi-brex.html|title=Nikoloz Tskitishvili leaves Tochigi Brex|date=December 24, 2015|work=Sportando.com|access-date=December 24, 2015}}</ref>

The next day, he returned to [[Champville SC|Champville]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/185964/nikoloz-tskitishvili-officially-inks-with-champville.html|title=Nikoloz Tskitishvili officially inks with Champville|date=December 25, 2015|work=Sportando.com|access-date=December 25, 2015}}</ref> On April 3, 2016, he left Champville, and signed with [[Chemidor Tehran BC|Chemidor Tehran]], of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://new.tehrantimes.com/news/300266/Iran-s-Chemidor-signs-Georgian-Nikoloz-Tskitishvili|title=Iran's Chemidor signs Georgian Nikoloz Tskitishvili|date=April 3, 2016|work=New.TehranTimes.com|access-date=April 9, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422191033/http://new.tehrantimes.com/news/300266/Iran-s-Chemidor-signs-Georgian-Nikoloz-Tskitishvili|archive-date=April 22, 2016}}</ref>

In late December 2017, he signed with [[Byblos Club]], of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Byblos sign Nikoloz Tskitishvili, ex Dinamo Tbilisi|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/517672/Byblos-sign-Nikoloz-Tskitishvili,-ex-Dinamo-Tbilisi|access-date=January 4, 2018|work=Eurobasket.com|date=December 29, 2017}}</ref>
